sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The global pivot toward Electric Vehicles (EVs) is touted as the definitive solution to the climate crisis. While the absence of tailpipe emissions is a tangible benefit, a "cradle-to-grave" analysis reveals a more nuanced reality. The production of EV batteries is resource-intensive, relying on the extraction of lithium, cobalt, and nickel—processes often marred by ecological destruction and human rights abuses in mining regions. Moreover, an EV is only as clean as the grid that charges it; driving an electric car in a coal-dependent economy merely shifts the pollution source from the highway to the power plant. Therefore, EVs are not a silver bullet but a transitional technology. True sustainability requires a simultaneous decarbonization of the energy grid and the development of circular economies for battery recycling.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Pollution in the contemporary world has emerged not merely as an environmental concern but as a reflection of flawed development priorities. Rapid industrialization and unplanned urban expansion have increased the discharge of harmful substances into air, water, and soil. Unlike visible disasters, pollution often progresses silently, accumulating over time before its consequences become evident. Air pollution contributes to chronic respiratory illnesses, while polluted water systems disrupt ecosystems and human health alike. Economic growth frequently takes precedence over ecological protection, weakening regulatory enforcement. Although environmental laws exist, they are often undermined by political pressures and corporate interests. Technological innovations offer temporary relief but rarely address the underlying causes of excessive production and consumption. Public participation in pollution control remains limited, as responsibility is largely shifted to authorities. Consequently, pollution persists as a systemic issue requiring structural, behavioral, and institutional transformation.

questions.q: A "cradle-to-grave" analysis refers to:
opts: The total environmental impact from raw-material extraction to disposal.
The journey from showroom to scrapyard.
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: a whole-life-cycle assessment. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: "An EV is only as clean as the grid that charges it" means:
opts: Charging stations must be kept clean.
If the electricity comes from fossil fuels, the EV still pollutes indirectly.
questions.why: Detail: pollution shifts 'from the highway to the power plant'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The author describes EVs as:
opts: A silver bullet for climate change.
A dangerous technology to be banned.
A transitional technology, not a complete solution.
questions.why: Detail: 'not a silver bullet but a transitional technology'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: What ethical concern about EV batteries is mentioned?
opts: Their production involves human rights abuses in mining regions.
questions.why: Detail: the third sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The tone of the passage can best be described as:
questions.why: Tone: accepts the benefit but corrects the hype. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The passage primarily argues that pollution is best understood as
opts: a temporary side effect of modernization
an unavoidable outcome of industrial growth
a systemic problem rooted in development patterns
questions.why: Main idea: 'a reflection of flawed development priorities' and 'a systemic issue'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: What does the phrase "progresses silently" suggest about pollution?
opts: It goes unnoticed until damage accumulates
It is easy to control early
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: 'accumulating over time before its consequences become evident'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, environmental laws fail mainly because
opts: enforcement is weakened by political and corporate interests
questions.why: Detail: the sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: The author’s criticism of technological solutions implies that
opts: pollution has deeper social and economic causes
questions.why: Inference: technology 'rarely address[es] the underlying causes'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: The overall tone of the passage can best be described as
questions.why: Tone: it analyses causes and criticises priorities. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: He spoke as if he were the owner of the house.
He spoke as if he is the owner of the house.
He spoke as if he being the owner of the house.
He spoke as if he will be the owner of the house.
questions.why: 'As if / as though' for an unreal situation takes the past subjunctive 'were'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Spot the error: “Unless you do not submit the form, you cannot sit the exam.”
questions.why: 'Unless' already means 'if not'; drop 'do not'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “Let us wait for the doctor.”
opts: He told to wait for the doctor.
He suggested that let them wait for the doctor.
He suggested that they should wait for the doctor.
He said that let us wait for the doctor.
questions.why: 'Let us' becomes 'suggested/proposed that they should'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “The train ______ before we reached the station.”
questions.why: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the conjunction relationship: “Walk carefully, lest you should fall.”
questions.why: 'Lest … should' expresses a negative purpose (so that … not). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.why: Launched by the Vice-President in August 2026.

questions.q: The second National Campaign on Entrepreneurship under DAY-NRLM (Aug–Nov 2026) aims to train:
Harsh Singh won a gold medal at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games in:
questions.why: Asmita Dey also won judo gold. Aug 2026.

questions.q: Shreyas Iyer reached a career-best rank in October 2026 in the ICC Men's T20I batting rankings. What rank?
August Kranti Diwas (8 August) marks Gandhi's 'Do or Die' call for the:
questions.why: 2026 was its 84th anniversary.

questions.q: Konkani was made the official language of Goa by the:
opts: Goa, Daman and Diu Official Language Act, 1987
questions.why: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani to the Eighth Schedule.

questions.q: 'Malabar' is a naval exercise among India and the navies of:
questions.why: The Quad navies.

questions.q: The Vikram-1 rocket is developed by which Indian private company?
questions.why: Skyroot is India's first space unicorn.

questions.q: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 went to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for work on:
Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in:
questions.why: A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, ?
questions.why: The terms are 1x2, 2x3, 3x4 and so on. The next is 7 x 8 = 56.

questions.q: In the word PANCHAYAT, how many letters lie between the first A and the last A?
questions.why: The first A is the 2nd letter and the last A is the 8th. Between them are N, C, H, A, Y: five letters.

questions.q: In a certain code MONDAY is 6, TUESDAY is 7 and WEDNESDAY is 9. What is SATURDAY in that code?
questions.why: Each word is coded by the number of letters in it. SATURDAY has 8.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: The first three are appointed revenue officials. A Sarpanch is an elected head of a Panchayat.

questions.q: A woman introduces a man as the son of her mother's brother. How is the man related to the woman?
questions.why: Her mother's brother is her uncle, and his son is her cousin.

questions.q: Sita's house faces south. She leaves by the back door, walks 50 m straight ahead, turns right and walks 30 m. In which direction is she walking now?
questions.why: The back of the house faces north. She walks north, and a right turn takes her east.

questions.q: Statement: "The company's profits have increased since the new advertising campaign." Which judgment is sound?
opts: The rise is solely due to the campaign
The rise is unrelated to the campaign
The campaign may have contributed to the rise
questions.why: Timing alone shows a possible link, not sole cause. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: Numbers: 325 618 378 461 782 562 213. If the 1st and 3rd digits of each are interchanged, what is the sum of the product of the 1st and 3rd digits of the lowest number and that of the highest number?
questions.why: New numbers: 523 816 873 164 287 265 312. Lowest 164 → 1 × 4 = 4; highest 873 → 8 × 3 = 24; total 28. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: agnoscrenia = poisonous spider; delanocrenia = poisonous snake; agnosdeery = brown spider. Which word could mean "black widow spider"?
questions.why: agnos = spider and comes first; the new word must start with agnos and use no known word. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: The diagonal of a rectangle is 25 cm and one side is 24 cm. Find its area.
questions.why: Other side √(625 − 576) = 7; area 24 × 7 = 168. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: The observation that symptoms disappear from above downward, from within outward and in the reverse order of their appearance is known as:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Constantine Hering described this direction of cure.

questions.q: According to §16, the vital force can be affected only by:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §16: being spirit-like, it can be deranged and restored only by dynamic influences.

questions.q: The return of old symptoms after a remedy is, according to Kent:
opts: a good sign that the disease is being cured
a sign the remedy was wrong
a reason to change the remedy at once
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Old symptoms reappearing means the cure is following the right direction; the remedy is left to act.

questions.q: Which miasm did Hahnemann call the oldest, most universal and the mother of countless chronic diseases (§80)?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §80: psora is the oldest, most universal and most pernicious chronic miasmatic disease.

questions.q: Ferrum phosphoricum is chiefly used in:
opts: the first stage of inflammations and fevers, before exudation
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ferrum phos: early inflammatory stage, haemorrhagic tendency.

questions.q: Varicose veins, bone affections and complaints that are better from cold and worse from heat, in a syphilitic constitution, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Fluoric acid: warm-blooded, varicosities, bone decay.

questions.q: Sour-smelling diarrhoea with green, frothy stools like the scum of a frog pond, in milk-intolerant infants, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Magnesia carb: sourness of the whole body.

questions.q: Bacillinum, a tubercular nosode, is especially used for:
opts: patients with a tubercular history and recurrent chest infections or ringworm
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Burnett introduced Bacillinum.

questions.q: Remedies such as X-ray, Magnetis polus and Sol are drawn from which source?
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Imponderabilia are 'weightless' energies: X-ray, magnetism, sunlight, electricity.

questions.q: The abbreviation 'p.r.n.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Pro re nata.

questions.q: The 'Complete Repertory' was compiled by:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Schroyens compiled Synthesis.

questions.q: C. M. Boger's approach to repertorisation gave special importance to:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Boger used pathological generals and causation.

questions.q: Secretin stimulates the pancreas to secrete juice rich in:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Cholecystokinin stimulates enzyme secretion and gallbladder contraction.

questions.q: Cortisol is secreted by the adrenal cortex zone called:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Glomerulosa = aldosterone; reticularis = androgens.

questions.q: Lines of Zahn indicate:
opts: a thrombus formed in flowing blood (ante-mortem)
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Alternating platelet–fibrin and red-cell layers.

questions.q: Kala-azar is transmitted by the:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Leishmania donovani; LD bodies in splenic aspirate.

questions.q: In a patient with Graves' disease, the thyroid profile shows (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Suppressed TSH with raised T3 and T4.

questions.q: The Koebner phenomenon (lesions appearing at sites of injury) is typical of:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Also seen in lichen planus and vitiligo.

questions.q: Urticaria with burning, stinging wheals, worse from heat and better from cold applications, calls for:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Apis: oedematous, stinging wheals, thirstless, better from cold.

questions.q: Oligomenorrhoea, hirsutism, acne and multiple small ovarian follicles on ultrasound suggest:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rotterdam criteria: two of anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries.

questions.q: Lower abdominal pain, fever, purulent vaginal discharge and cervical motion tenderness suggest:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. PID is an ascending infection; it risks infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

questions.q: For blunt injuries, bruises and a sore, bruised feeling after a fall, the first remedy is:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Arnica is the trauma remedy for blunt injury and shock.

questions.q: Punctured wounds that feel cold to touch yet are better from cold applications call for:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Ledum: puncture wounds, insect bites; cold yet better by cold.

questions.q: The main objective of Tele-MANAS is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. National Tele Mental Health Programme, launched in 2022.

questions.q: The core principle of the Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
opts: Health for All through primary health care
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Primary health care as the key.
